items.note: `ds-table`'s boolean `clientSort` is REMOVED and replaced by `sortMode: 'client' | 'server' | 'none'`. The boolean could not express "nothing sorts", so a column marked `sortable: true` on a table with no sorting drew a header that looked live, showed a caret on hover and did nothing — mm-broker shipped several detail tables that way and only caught it in a browser walkthrough. ACTION, mechanical: `[clientSort]="true"` becomes `sortMode="client"`; a bare `clientSort` attribute becomes `sortMode="client"`; `[clientSort]="false"` or `[clientSort]="expr"` becomes `[sortMode]="expr ? 'client' : 'server'"`. A table that had NO clientSort binding and reorders in its own `(sortChange)` handler must now say `sortMode="server"` — this is the one case that is not a find/replace, because the DEFAULT CHANGED: unset now resolves to `'client'`, so a table that previously only emitted `sortChange` will ALSO sort its own rows unless it declares `'server'`. That default flip is deliberate — it makes `sortable: true` always do something — but for a SERVER-PAGED table (one that binds `total`) client sorting reorders the current page only, so the rows look sorted and are not; dev builds warn about exactly that combination. Tables that render a sortable column but sort nowhere should declare `sortMode="none"`, which now drops the button, the caret and `aria-sort` instead of leaving a dead control.

The exported `FieldMessageState` union gained `'warning'` ('default' | 'error' | 'warning' | 'success'). ACTION only for code that switches EXHAUSTIVELY over it — a `switch` with no `default`, or a mapped type keyed by the union, stops compiling until the `'warning'` arm exists. Assigning or comparing single values is unaffected.

All 14 message-bearing field classes changed their member surface, which breaks a consumer who EXTENDS one (subclassing a DS component is unsupported — design-system.md § Components — but where it happens the names collide: TS4114 demands `override`, TS2415 fires on a redeclared private member). REMOVED: the protected `messageState` computed on every field, plus `messageText` on DatePickerComponent. ADDED on all 14: `error`, `warning`, `errors`, `touched` inputs, plus `message` and `invalidResolved`; DatePickerComponent also gained the private `localError` and `dateInvalid`; the two CVA base classes (`DsControlValueAccessor`, `DsBooleanControlValueAccessor`) gained a protected `touchedSelf`. AppLayoutComponent gained public `railOverlay` and `railId`. ACTION: rename the subclass's own member, or add `override` where the base's semantics genuinely match; a subclass that overrode `messageState` should move its logic to an `error` / `warning` binding on the element instead, since the message is now resolved centrally. Consumers who only use the <ds-...> elements need no change.

STYLING ONLY, and only for a consumer who styles ds-select's internal DOM. The label element is now `.label`, the same class every other field in the family uses, so a rule written as `.select-label` (or the doubled `.select-label.select-label` needed to out-rank the shimmed component rule) silently matches nothing after the upgrade. Retarget to `.label`, scoped to the element: `ds-select .label { … }`. In most cases the rule can be DELETED instead — it existed to make the select's label match the input's, and they now match by default. Scope strictly to selectors under ds-select; `.label` is also the class ds-input, ds-textarea, ds-date-picker, ds-time-picker and ds-radio-group use.

TWO changes to the same element. (1) CLASS: `ds-radio-group`'s label is now `.label`, so consumer CSS targeting `.group-label` under ds-radio-group stops matching — retarget or delete. Note `.group-label` is ALSO the class `ds-sidenav-group` uses for its heading, which is unchanged; only rules scoped under ds-radio-group are affected. (2) VISIBLE: the label now draws the family's type - `--font-weight-bold` at `--font-size-xs` - instead of its own `--font-weight-medium` at `--font-size-s` on `--line-height-flat`. It was the only field label drawing its own, and in a form beside an input or select it read as a different kind of element. ACTION: none for most screens, since matching the family is the point. To keep the old look, scope the family tokens: `ds-radio-group { --ds-field-label-weight: var(--font-weight-medium); --ds-field-label-font-size: var(--font-size-s); }`.

`ng add` never actually ran its schematic in any released version, so the DS global styles were NEVER wired automatically - every consumer either did it by hand or shipped without them. The package is `"type": "module"` while the compiled schematic was CommonJS, so Node refused to load it: "exports is not defined in ES module scope". The build wrote a nested schematics/package.json with {"type":"commonjs"} to fix exactly that, and `npm pack` silently DROPPED it - npm treats a directory holding a package.json as a separate package root - so the marker existed in dist/ and was absent from the tarball. The schematic is now `.cts` compiled to `.cjs`, which survives packing. ACTION: consumers who added `@use '@ids-group-ltd/ids-design-system/styles/ds';` to their global stylesheet by hand need do nothing - ng add prepends the same line and skips when it is already present. Consumers who never wired the styles (and whose components therefore render unthemed) can now run `ng add` and have it work, or add that one line themselves.

informational: Every field gained `error` and `warning` beside `hint`, resolved on a fixed ladder: `error` (an explicit string, shown at once) → validation errors → `warning` → `hint`. Only ONE line renders, so a field's height does not depend on how many sources are populated. Purely additive: a field that binds only `hint` behaves exactly as before, and when something is invalid but no source produced text the `hint` still renders in the error state — so the pre-existing `[invalid]` + `[hint]="errorText"` idiom keeps working untouched.

Fields now read validation state from the bound form control, so `error` is optional. Signal forms binds `errors` and `touched` automatically (those input names are Angular 21's `FormUiControl` contract) and already drove the value through the `ControlValueAccessor` DS fields have always implemented. Reactive and template-driven forms need NO new binding: the field resolves `NgControl` after first render and subscribes to `control.events`. Errors wait for the first blur, or for the parent form to be submitted, so a `required` error never greets an untouched form. `invalid` is now OR-ed with what the control reports; the explicit input still wins.

`DS_CONFIG` gained `field.errorMessages` — one shared map from validation-error kind to text, for errors whose validator carried no message (Angular's built-ins never do). A message on the error itself always wins, so `required(path, { message })` in signal forms or `{ myError: 'text' }` from a plain validator overrides the map per case. An error that resolves to no text anywhere warns in dev instead of rendering an error style with an empty line.

`dsRailTrigger` is a new directive: put it on your own burger anywhere inside `ds-app-layout` and it toggles `[(railOpen)]` and keeps `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls` pointing at the rail panel, so the trigger and the panel are related for a screen reader. Both attributes are dropped while the rail is not an overlay, where `aria-expanded="false"` would contradict what the user sees. `ds-app-layout` also exposes `railId` and the read-only `railOverlay` signal for a consumer that builds its own trigger.

`ds-table` `sortMode="none"` is the way to render a column that is sortable in principle but not on this screen: the header renders as plain text, with no button, caret or `aria-sort`, instead of a control that does nothing.

Bugfix, no action: a CLOSED compact `ds-app-layout` rail is now `inert`, and closing it (Escape, scrim click, navigation) returns focus to the control that claims the rail via `aria-controls`. Before, the off-canvas panel kept `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal="true"`, left every nav link tabbable and stranded the caret inside the hidden panel, because cdkTrapFocusAutoCapture restores focus only on directive destroy. A consumer whose custom burger sets neither `dsRailTrigger` nor `aria-controls` gets the inert fix but no focus return - add `aria-controls` pointing at `ds-app-layout`'s `railId` to get it.

Bugfix, no action: `--ds-overlay-enter-scale` is now forwarded onto the portaled overlay pane, so scoping it per instance (`ds-select { --ds-overlay-enter-scale: 0.9; }`) finally reaches select / multi-select / autocomplete / date / time / colour picker / popover / tooltip / menu-submenu panels. 0.7.1 shipped it as a known gap — the token was resolved on the pane but absent from the forwarded set, while the other four enter tokens did forward. A GLOBAL override worked before and is unaffected.

The field family gained one label contract: --ds-field-label-font-size / -weight / -color / -transform / -tracking, resolved by ds-input, ds-textarea, ds-select, ds-date-picker, ds-time-picker and ds-radio-group through a shared mixin. Defaults equal the values those components hard-coded, so nothing moves unless you set a token. There is deliberately no per-component token set - custom-property scoping already narrows a retune to one element (`ds-select { --ds-field-label-transform: uppercase; }`) - and -transform/-tracking make the uppercase tracked label reachable through tokens for the first time. ds-input's --ds-input-label-color/-fs/-fw still take precedence where set and now fall through to the family token rather than the raw scale.

`--ds-field-height` is new, and the --field-h-sm/-md/-lg scale is now actually read by ds-input, ds-select, ds-date-picker and ds-time-picker - previously only -lg was, the other two sizes reaching past the scale to the raw --hit-min/--hit-cozy. Values are identical, so no height moves on upgrade. NO ACTION, but two things become possible that silently did nothing before: retuning --field-h-md (or -sm) now moves every field, and --ds-field-height pins one height regardless of the size class, scopable per component. NOT a fix for unequal picker heights - those were already equal as of 0.7.1's aligned trigger geometry.

ds-button gained --ds-button-font-size / -weight / -tracking / -height / -pad-x / -pad-y, and reflects data-variant / data-color on its host element for external targeting. Defaults equal the hard-coded values, so nothing moves. NO ACTION - but a consumer who wrote .button.button.button { font-size; font-weight; letter-spacing; padding; height } to out-rank the shimmed .button.md can replace it with the tokens, set on the host. Per-variant --ds-button-* values were ALREADY reachable from the host before this change (the colour/fill resolvers read the hook first and never declare it), so an indirection layer added to work around that can go too.

ds-app-layout gained opt-in restoreScroll + restoreScrollTimeout, and LayoutScrollService gained contentReady() and consumePendingOffset(). Off by default, so NO ACTION. Turn it on for a list-and-details app and going back returns the reader to their place; forward links still land at the top. A 'back to list' control that adds a history entry instead of traversing must pass state: { dsRestoreScroll: true } to be restored. Note that an app which scrolls on navigation itself (an anchor jump, a URL that names a section) writes after the layout and wins, so restoreScroll is a no-op on those routes.

New role layer between the foundation scales and components: --ds-radius-{inner,control,panel,pill}, --ds-elevation-{raised,overlay,floating,modal}, and --ds-motion-{enter-panel,enter-surface,enter-large,exit,exit-large}-{duration,easing}. Every role defaults to the value its members already used, so NO ACTION and nothing moves visually. What becomes possible: retune one family without hitting the others - re-round panels while buttons keep their radius, lift every overlay in one line, make panel entrances snappier once. The old --shadow-popover/-modal/-toast/-card aliases still work and now resolve THROUGH the elevation roles. A per-component --ds-<comp>-radius / -shadow / -enter-duration override still wins over its role. Note: two motion resolvers (ds-loading-overlay, the toast leave) deliberately stay on the raw scale because they use --ease-standard, which no role carries.

New global focus-style switch: set data-focus="ring" | "field" | "edge" | "outline" on <html>. Omitting it keeps the current split (halo on fields, double ring on controls), so NO ACTION. A-la-carte consumers who @use DS partials individually must add `@use 'styles/focus';` to get the switch and the forced-colors fallback; consumers of the bundled `styles/ds` entry get both automatically. Also new, and not part of the switch: under @media (forced-colors: active) every focused element gets a CanvasText outline, because forced-colors drops box-shadow and a shadow-only focus indicator disappeared there entirely.

ds-table gained [persistLayout] + storageKey (round-tripping columnOrder, columnWidths and hiddenKeys through localStorage) and [exportButton] + exportFilename + exportFetcher. All opt-in and off by default, so NO ACTION. A consumer who wrote their own localStorage effect for the three column models, or their own export button, can delete both - together with the sortValue accessor these were the last three reasons to keep a wrapper around ds-table. exportCsv() is unchanged for existing callers and now accepts an optional row set as its second argument.

New component ds-password-rules: the live requirement checklist under a new-password field. Purely additive, NO ACTION. A consumer with a hand-rolled password checklist can replace it - pass the rule set as { label, test } pairs (the policy stays yours, it has to mirror your server), bind [value] to the field and [showUnmet] to whether the user has tried to submit. Exposes metCount and allMet for gating a submit button.

ds-input gained ariaDescribedBy, merged with the field's own message id rather than replacing it - for describing a field with a password-rule list or a policy note. Additive, NO ACTION. Note that setting aria-describedby on the <ds-input> element itself does NOT work: it lands on the wrapper, not the inner input.

New component ds-auth-shell: the scaffold for the screens in front of the login (sign-in, forgot password, reset, MFA), counterpart to ds-app-layout. Purely additive, NO ACTION. A consumer with a hand-rolled auth scaffold can replace it: brand lockup + optional tagline + one card holding the form + a support line. The brand row is the ds-sidenav row - same brand / logoLetter / [dsBrandName] contract and the same letter-mark tile - so it is NOT the string-splitting brandAccent the ports used; project [dsBrandName] to tint a slice of the wordmark. Card body is the default slot, the support line goes in [dsAuthSupport] (a real <footer>, so it carries the contentinfo landmark). cardElevation / cardPadding pass through to ds-card. Tokens: --ds-auth-shell-min-height, -card-max-width, -gap, -bg-color, -mark-bg-color, -mark-label-color. WORTH KNOWING when porting: the shell owns the full-height box itself, so do NOT wrap it in your own 100vh/100dvh container - the ports that stacked two scrolled a page whose content fits. It also adds env(safe-area-inset-*) padding, and centres with auto margins rather than centre alignment so a form taller than the box stays reachable when the shell is embedded at min-height 100%.
